{{Quote|Welcome to Boz Pity…I read it's some sort of graveyard planet. But the size of the memorials…|Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="SWO4" />}}
'''Boz Pity''' was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Boz Pity system/Legends|Boz Pity system]] of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]. It was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Gargantelle]] [[Species/Legends|species]], noted for their large stature. When the planet was discovered at some point before the end of the [[Ductavis Era]], the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] attempted to [[Slavery/Legends|enslave]] the species. After the Gargantelles repelled seven invasions and four [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] missions, the Hutts convinced the [[Electric Caliph]]s of Boz Pity's neighbor world [[Mourn]] to exterminate the species. The Gargantelles were slowly driven to extinction over the next decade, but erected a substantial amount of enormous gravestones to their fallen. When the species disappeared, these monuments earned Boz Pity the nickname "'''the graveyard planet'''," which prompted inhabitants of nearby systems to travel to the planet to bury their dead.

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] used the planet as a staging point for raids on the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] borders, and constructed a [[Boz Pity Confederacy base|large base]] on Boz Pity's surface. In [[19 BBY/Legends|19.43 BBY]], towards the end of the war, Republic forces [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|seized]] control of the planet. Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] established a base on the planet. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] discovered the base shortly after, and launched an [[Battle of Boz Pity (Galactic Civil War)/Legends|attack]] on Boz Pity, but the Alliance was able to evacuate.

Between [[25 ABY/Legends|25]] and [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], the Boz Pity system was attacked by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] during their [[Yuuzhan Vong War|attempt]] at conquering [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] forces drove them out between [[27 ABY/Legends|27]] and [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]].

==Description==
[[File:BozPityconcept.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Gargantelle ruins on Boz Pity]]
Boz Pity was situated in the [[Boz Pity system/Legends|Boz Pity system]] of the [[Halla sector/Legends|Halla sector]],<ref name="TEAOC" /> near the border of the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] and the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. The only nearby [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] was the [[Ilosian Spur/Legends|Ilosian Spur]], which connected the [[Lesser Lantillian Route/Legends|Lesser Lantillian Route]] with [[Pabol Sleheyron/Legends|Pabol Sleheyron]] in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]].<ref name="TEAp" /> It was locked in synchronous [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]] around the [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Cama Coll]] with [[Mourn]], a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] that was enshrouded in smoke.<ref name="TEAp" />

After the extinction of the native [[Gargantelle]] [[Species/Legends|species]], Boz Pity was entirely without [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] life. The [[Death/Legends|death]] monuments erected by the species were a prominent terrain feature, and ensured Boz Pity the nickname "the graveyard planet." Inhabitants of nearby systems would also bury their dead on the planet.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|90|Boz Pity}}</ref> Apart from the many graves, the terrain was dominated by rocky fields, sand-filled valleys<ref name="TEAp" /> and grassy fields,<ref name="SWO4" /> dotted with mountains.<ref name="TEAp" />

[[Politics/Legends|Politically]], the only major power to truly establish a presence on the planet was the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]].<ref name="SWO4" /> After driving the Confederacy away late in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had some military forces stationed there.<ref name="SWDT6" />

==History==
===Early history===
Boz Pity was [[Homeworld/Legends|home]] to the sentient Gargantelle species. When the planet was discovered by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] of [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Nal Hutta]] between [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000]] and [[9000 BBY]],<ref name="TEAn1">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''; The Galactic Explorations map marks the area of space containing Boz Pity as discovered between 15,000 and 8,000 BBY. The planet entry mentions that the planet was known since the [[Ductavis Era]], which ended in 9000 BBY.</ref> they identified the Gargantelles as viable [[Slavery/Legends|slaves]], largely due to the species' massive stature. A series of missions were launched to attempt to enslave them—seven invasions by [[Nikto/Legends|Niktos]], followed by four [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] attempts by [[t'landa Til]]—but they all ended the same way: the Hutt servants were eaten by the natives. This infuriated the Hutt overlords, and prompted them to concoct a new plan. Instead of enslaving the Gargantelles, they would exterminate them. A legal team of [[Nimbanel/Legends|Nimbanels]] was sent to Boz Pity's neighbor world Mourn to recruit the services of the [[Electric Caliph]]s—ten-millennia-old [[Droid/Legends|droids]] that once belonged to [[Sultan/Legends|Sultan]] [[Nastuonodon]]. By appealing to their sense of obsolescence, the Nimbanels successfully convinced the caliphs to rid Boz Pity of sentient life. Over the next decade, the Gargantelles were slowly driven extinct. The species erected enormous monuments to their fallen, which would later contribute to Boz Pity's reputation as a "graveyard planet." When the last Gargantelle died, the caliphs returned to Mourn and set the planet's crust on fire, killing themselves.<ref name="TEAp" />

===The Clone Wars===
{{Quote|Saleucami has fallen, and Master Vos has moved his troops to Boz Pity.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:Battleofbozpity.jpg|thumb|left|160px|The Battle of Boz Pity.]]
During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], Boz Pity was occupied by the Confederacy of Independent Systems to serve as a staging point for raids on the Galactic Republic's borders.<ref name="TEAp" /> A [[Boz Pity Confederacy base|large base]] was constructed on the planet, and over a hundred [[Warship/Legends|warships]] were stationed in the system. The Republic discovered the Separatist presence when [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] prompted a search of the system, hoping to find the Confederacy [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Asajj Ventress/Legends|Asajj Ventress]].<ref name="SWO4" />

In 19.43 BBY,<ref name="NECp">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Republic forces assaulted Boz Pity. Several [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] who were assigned to the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] participated in the assault. An attempt was made to sneak the ''[[Intervention]]''—a [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyer]]—past the Separatist [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] by having it exit [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] between the fleet and the planet. The plan backfired, however,<ref name="SWO4" /> and the ensuing [[Battle of Boz Pity (Clone Wars)|Battle of Boz Pity]] proved bloody.<ref name="SWO5">[[Obsession 5|''Obsession'' 5]]</ref> The ''Intervention'' crash-landed on Boz Pity, where the Jedi found themselves in a land battle against forces under the command<ref name="SWO4" /> of the Confederacy leader<ref name="ROTSN">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref> [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], as well as [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]].<ref name="SWO4" /> Republic naval officer [[Denn Wessex]] commanded the ''Venator''-class ''[[Redoubt]]'' in the battle over the planet.<ref name="HNN">{{InsiderCite|84|Republic HoloNet News Special Inaugural Edition 16:5:241}}</ref> Although suffering major losses, the Republic won the battle, but the Separatist leadership was able to evacuate the planet.<ref name="SWO5" />

Following the battle, the Republic maintained a presence on Boz Pity.<ref name="SWDT6" /> After the [[Siege of Saleucami/Legends|Siege of Saleucami]], the Jedi [[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] moved his force of [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] to the planet.<ref name="DBSa">{{DB|location|saleucami|Saleucami}}</ref> Following the Clone Wars, planets in the region continued to take their dead to Boz Pity.<ref name="EOTECR">[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Core Rulebook]]</ref>

[[File:BozPitytres.jpg|thumb|right|170px|The [[Battle of Boz Pity (Galactic Civil War)/Legends|showdown]] between the Alliance and the Empire]]

===Galactic Civil War===
In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] was forced to relocate from their base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. A list put together by<ref name="SWBRS" /> [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaanian]] [[Viceroy/Legends|Viceroy]]<ref name="DBBO">{{DB|character|bailorgana|Organa, Bail}}</ref> and Alliance member [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] named Boz Pity as a viable location for a new base. After sending a survey team to the planet, the Alliance established a base among the ruins of the Gargantelle buildings. The base would prove short-lived: not long after it was established, the Alliance's elite [[Renegade Squadron/Legends|Renegade Squadron]] was tracked to the planet through an [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Homing beacon/Legends|tracking beacon]]. The Empire immediately launched an attack on the base, deploying a large amount of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], several [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]], and one [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transport]]. However, in the ensuing [[Battle of Boz Pity (Galactic Civil War)/Legends|battle]], Renegade Squadron was able to keep the Imperial forces at bay long enough for the Rebel Alliance to evacuate the planet.<ref name="SWBRS" /> Between [[4 ABY/Legends|4]] and [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Boz Pity was under the hegemony of Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Treuten Teradoc]]'s [[Greater Maldrood]] faction. Between [[25 ABY/Legends|25]] and [[26 ABY/Legends|26 ABY]], the Boz Pity system was attacked by the [[Yuuzhan Vong]], an [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] species.<ref name="TEAp" /> The system remained under their control until between [[27 ABY/Legends|27]] and [[29 ABY/Legends|29 ABY]], when [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] forces arrived.<ref name="TEAp" />

==Inhabitants==
[[File:Skullofbigsize.jpg|thumb|left|A Gargantelle skull]]
{{Main|Gargantelle}}
The Gargantelles were the only sentient species native to Boz Pity. They were a particularly large species; individuals could reach a height of twenty [[Meter/Legends|meters]], and they were equipped with six [[Limb/Legends|arms]]. These traits made them desirable slaves to the Hutts. They were fierce warriors, able to resist almost a dozen attempts at enslavement through sheer force. One of their traditions was to erect very large gravestones for their fallen.<ref name="TEAp" /> After their extinction, Gargantelle [[Skeleton/Legends|skeletons]] littered the surface of Boz Pity.<ref name="SWO4" />

==Behind the scenes==
Boz Pity first appeared in [[Obsession 3|issue #3]] of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series ''[[Star Wars: Obsession]]'' ([[2005]]), written by [[W. Haden Blackman]]. It was subsequently mentioned in several ''[[Star Wars]]'' works; perhaps most notably in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] (2005).

''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' ([[2009]]) substantially fleshed out the planet. Co-authors [[Jason Fry]] and [[Daniel Wallace]] wanted to include profiles for all the planets mentioned in ''Revenge of the Sith'', which included Boz Pity. The story of the Gargantelles was invented for the ''Atlas'', and the species' name was a reference to [[Wikipedia:Gargantua and Pantagruel|''Gargantua and Pantagruel'']], a 16th century series of novels by [[Wikipedia:François Rabelais|François Rabelais]]. The Electric Caliphs, an invention of Wallace's for ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'', were tied into the history of Boz Pity.<ref name="TEAend">{{Blog|danwallace|145|Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 3 of 5)}}</ref>

When designing the planet for use in ''[[Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron]]'', artist [[Mark Harrison]] drew inspiration from ancient [[Wikipedia:Cambodia|Cambodian]] architecture. The temple complex [[Wikipedia:Angkor Wat|Angkor Wat]] was a particularly big influence.<ref name="GS">{{WebCite|url=http://www.gamespot.com/pages/unions/read_article.php?topic_id=25852853&union_id=14038|text=Boz Pity|author=Mike Rosser|date=2007-08-15|archiveurl=https://archive.is/OqOL3|nolive=1}}</ref> Particular attention was given to the world's status as a "graveyard world"—concept art for Boz Pity included drawings of elaborate headstones and enormous skeletons with three faces.<ref name="RLp">''[[Rogue Leaders: The Story of LucasArts]]''</ref> ''Star Wars Battlefront: Renegade Squadron'' erroneously identifies Boz Pity as an Outer Rim planet.<ref name="SWBRS" />
